in_arabic.name: هميدة
in_arabic.long_meaning: هميدة هي اسم علم مؤنث عربي يعود إلى الجذر همد، الذي يعني الجمال والخير والبركة، ويرتبط بال女性 الجميلات والطيبات، ذكرت في كتب التراث الإسلامي كاسم لنساء طيبات ومُحسنت، ويعتبر من الأسماء المُحببة في الثقافة الإسلامية لما يحمله من معاني إيجابية

in_urdu.name: حمیدہ
in_urdu.long_meaning: حمیدہ ایک عربی نام ہے جو عرب کے جڑھ همد سے ماخوذ ہے، جس کا مطلب ہے خوبصورتی اور نیک خاتون، اسلامی روایت میں یہ نام نیک عورتوں کے لیے استعمال ہوا ہے، اور جنوبی ایشیائی مسلم ثقافت میں بہت پسند کیا جاتا ہے

in_hindi.name: हमीदा
in_hindi.long_meaning: हमीदा एक अरबी नाम है जो अरबी जड़ همد से लिया गया है, जिसका अर्थ है सुंदरता और अच्छाई, इस्लामी परंपरा में यह नाम अच्छी महिलाओं के लिए उपयोग किया जाता है, और भारतीय मुस्लिम समुदाय में बहुत पसंद किया जाता है

in_pashto.name: حمیده
in_pashto.long_meaning: حمیده د عربي نوم دی چې د عربي ریښ همد څخه اخیستل شوی، چې معنا یې ښکلا او نېکمرغي ده، په اسلامي دود کې دا نوم نېکمرغو ښځو لپاره کارول کیږي، او په افغان/پښتنو دود کې ډېر غوره کیږي

in_english.name: Humayda
in_english.long_meaning: Humayda is an Arabic name derived from the root HMD, meaning beauty and goodness, it is used in Islamic tradition to refer to good women, and is significant in Muslim cultures for its positive connotations and spiritual meaning

data.cultural_impact: The name Humayda carries a rich cultural heritage, as it originated from the noble character of one of the most celebrated figures in Islamic history, Umm Humayda bint Abu Sahm. She is renowned for her remarkable resilience and courage, as she protected and defended her youngest son, Ali ibn Abi Talib (as), the fourth Caliph and the cousin of Prophet Muhammad (pbuh), during the Battle of Khaybar in 628 AD. This establishing mother-son bond formed a significant moment in the Islamic narrative as a model of maternal love, devotion, and fortitude—an image that still echoes and resonates in the Arab and Muslim worlds.
data.spiritual_significance: The Islamic name Humayda, steeped in significance and meaning, implies a deep spiritual connection to the ideals of praiseworthiness and devotion towards Allah. This resonance echoes the seminal English words 'to honor' and 'to be revered.' Derived from the root 'hamida,' it purports a lofty moral purpose that calls to bring the boon of blessings, accolades and divine attention to those who hold its essence, by extending compassion, kindness, and admiration to all beings.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Humayda bint Zayd ibn Harithah al-Khawla was a prominent figure in early Islamic history. The name Humayda carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: She was a warrior-woman, and a member of the Banu Khazraj tribe in Medina. She is best known for her role in the Battle of Uhud, where she fought alongside the Prophet Muhammad (pbuh).

modern_usage.modern_context: The name Humayda remains relevant in modern Muslim society, representing a bridge between traditional Islamic values and contemporary life. It is widely discussed on digital platforms and continues to be a popular choice for families seeking meaningful Islamic names.
